summary: Describes how to use the L2TPv3 control plane for Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) pseudowires, and gives guidelines for carrying various ATM services over an IP network. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: Old-style ATM phone lines get packed up and sent across the regular Internet, then unpacked at the other end, so the two ends act as if still wired together.

subtitle: How to carry ATM circuits across an IP network as L2TPv3 pseudowires, in packet or cell form.

tldr.problem: Providers needed to carry ATM services across an IP packet network while the two ATM ends still behave as if directly connected.
tldr.mechanism: Each ATM circuit maps to an L2TPv3 session, with an ATM-specific sublayer and either reassembled AAL5 frames or relayed ATM cells as the payload, plus new AVPs for status and alarms.
tldr.outcome: ATM AAL5, virtual channel, virtual path and port services can ride over IP, with stated limits on cell-level fidelity. RFC 5641 later updated this RFC.

sections.title: ATM Pseudowires over L2TPv3
sections.content:
This RFC explains how to use the Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol, Version 3 (L2TPv3) to emulate ATM pseudowires (ATMPWs). It covers the encapsulation, the ATM services that can be carried (AAL5 SDU, and ATM VCC, VPC and port cell relay), and the mapping of ATM defects to L2TP Set-Link-Info (SLI) messages that tell the peer endpoint (the LCCE).

ATM-specific attribute value pairs (AVPs) and other L2TP constructs are defined here. Switched and soft permanent virtual paths and connections (SVP/SVC, SPVP/SPVC) are out of scope. The reader is expected to know the terms of RFC 3931.
sections.plainLanguage: ATM is an old kind of network. This RFC explains how to make an ATM link seem to work even though its data is really traveling through the Internet.

sections.title: Setting Up and Tearing Down a Session
sections.content:
A control connection as in RFC 3931 MUST be established first. The SCCRQ and SCCRP messages MUST list the supported ATM pseudowire types in the Pseudowire Capabilities List, and each LCCE MUST identify itself with a globally unique value, by default the Router ID AVP.

Creating an ATM circuit (for example an AAL5 PVC) triggers an L2TP session using the three-way handshake of RFC 3931. An LCCE may start the session at once or wait until the circuit is ACTIVE. The ICRQ MUST carry a Remote End ID so the peer can match the session to its own circuit, and the Circuit Status AVP MUST be in the ICRQ and ICRP. If the peer has not provisioned the circuit, it answers with a CDN, and the first LCCE SHOULD retry periodically with a configurable period and maximum number of retries.

When an ATM circuit is deleted at either end, the session MUST be torn down with a CDN. Sessions use the L2TP Hello facility as keepalive, and SLI messages report later status changes.
sections.plainLanguage: It is like two friends each setting up a walkie-talkie. One says 'ready?', the other says 'ready!', and the first says 'great, go'. When one switches off, they say goodbye properly.

sections.title: Encapsulation and the ATM-Specific Sublayer
sections.content:
Each packet has the IP transport header, then the L2TP session header (a non-zero 32-bit Session ID with an optional cookie of up to 64 bits), then an ATM-specific sublayer, then the ATM payload. The sublayer is REQUIRED for AAL5 SDU mode and OPTIONAL for cell mode.

Besides the S bit (sequencing) and the B and E bits (fragmentation), it defines four flags:

  • T: set when the packet holds an ATM admin cell rather than an AAL5 payload.
  • G: carries the Explicit Forward Congestion Indication (EFCI) bit.
  • C: carries the Cell Loss Priority (CLP) bit.
  • U: carries the Frame Relay command/response bit from the AAL5 CPCS-UU field.

The L2-Specific Sublayer AVP gains a new value, 2, meaning the ATM-specific sublayer is used. Sequencing MAY be enabled, and then the ATM-specific sublayer must be requested.
sections.plainLanguage: Each parcel gets a small label saying whether it is a special message, whether the road is busy, and what number it is in the line.

sections.title: AAL5 Mode and Cell Relay Mode
sections.content:
In AAL5-SDU mode each AAL5 virtual circuit maps to one L2TP session. The ingress LCCE reassembles the AAL5 frame without its trailer and padding, and sends the CPCS-SDU. If it is too big for the session MTU, it may be fragmented as per [L2TPFRAG] or by the IP layer below. The pseudowire type is 0x0002.

In cell mode cells skip reassembly. Each cell is a 4-byte ATM header plus a 48-byte payload, without the HEC. One or several cells can share a packet, limited by the session MTU and by what the egress LCCE can process. Cell mode has three services: VCC relay (type 0x0009), VPC relay (type 0x000A) and port relay (type 0x0003). On a port, each LCCE MUST discard idle or unassigned cells.
sections.plainLanguage: One way is to unpack a whole letter and send only the words. The other way is to forward every little envelope exactly as it came, sometimes several in one bag.

sections.title: OAM Cells, Status and Alarms
sections.content:
OAM (operation, administration and maintenance) cells are always sent using cell mode encapsulation. For VCC switching, LCCEs SHOULD pass F5 OAM cells; for VPC switching they MUST pass F4 OAM cells and F5 cells transparently. In AAL5 mode, OAM cells arriving during reassembly are sent right away, so their order relative to user data is not kept. Performance monitoring and security OAM cells should not be used with AAL5 SDU mode, and may be dropped.

The OAM Emulation Required AVP (type 87) signals OAM emulation for AAL5 mode. If the peer cannot support it, the session MUST be torn down with a CDN carrying result code 22.

Circuit state travels in the Circuit Status AVP, whose A bit says ACTIVE (1) or INACTIVE (0) and whose N bit says new (1) or existing (0). The ATM Alarm Status AVP (type 88) adds a circuit status reason and an alarm type, such as AIS, RDI, LOS, LOP, LOF, loopback or continuity check. The ATM Maximum Concatenated Cells AVP (type 86) tells the sender how many cells it may pack in one packet.
sections.plainLanguage: Special check-up messages travel along with the data. If a line breaks, the two ends send each other a note that says which kind of problem it is.

sections.title: What Is and Is Not Preserved
sections.content:
ATMPWs are point-to-point. AAL5-SDU mode carries only PVC-based services, and several things are not carried across: per-cell EFCI and CLP values (only one G and one C bit per frame), all of the CPCS-UU field except its least significant bit, the CPI field, and the AAL5 CRC. The CRC is stripped at ingress and regenerated at egress, so errors added while crossing the network may go undetected. The RFC notes that IPsec can be used to protect payload integrity.

Cell relay mode can carry all AAL types. The ATM service payload is a multiple of 52 bytes, and the HEC is not carried, so header corruption in transit may also go undetected. OAM cells keep their order with user cells. Concatenating cells improves bandwidth efficiency but adds latency and delay variation, and concatenation and fragmentation should not be used together. In both modes, QoS can be supported by mapping ATM service categories to a PSN class of service.
sections.plainLanguage: Some small details on the original parcels get lost on the trip, so the RFC lists exactly which ones, so you know what to expect.

sections.title: Congestion Control
sections.content:
The IP network carrying a pseudowire can lose or delay packets, and some ATM services cannot slow down in response. Cell relay pseudowires should run over traffic-engineered networks where possible. On a best-effort network, pseudowires carrying CBR and VBR-rt traffic SHOULD be halted during acute congestion, while UBR pseudowires need not be halted and may have cells delayed or dropped.

LCCEs SHOULD watch for congestion, for example by measuring packet loss. If severe congestion is found, the ATM service SHOULD be ended by tearing down the session with a CDN. The pseudowire may be restarted manually or automatically after a suitable wait.
sections.plainLanguage: If the road is jammed, the delivery service for things that cannot wait may be stopped for a while so everyone else can still get through.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: ATM over L2TPv3 is subject to the security considerations of RFC 3931. The RFC says there are no additional considerations specific to carrying ATM that are not present when carrying other data link types.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new is risky here. The same safety rules as for the underlying tunnel protocol apply.
